headline: Nigeria Powers 100 Hospitals with Solar Energy
meta_description: Nigeria has already solar-powered about 100 hospitals, with a new financing framework targeting 30% of health facilities by 2027.
summary_short: Nigeria's ambitious solar initiative has already brought renewable energy to 100 hospitals, with plans to reach 30% of all health facilities by 2027.
body:
Nigeria has already solar-powered about 100 hospitals, expanding access to reliable energy in the healthcare system. A new government financing framework now aims to bring 24-hour electricity to 30% of health facilities by 2027, a significant step toward improving patient care across the country.

The shift toward solar power addresses a critical challenge: unreliable electricity has long hampered hospitals' ability to run essential equipment, refrigerate medicines, and maintain sterile conditions. By anchoring the expansion in a dedicated financing framework, the government is signaling long-term commitment to sustainability.

The scale of the goal—reaching 30% of facilities within five years—suggests momentum beyond individual projects. Each hospital powered by solar represents not just a facility upgrade, but improved outcomes for patients who depend on consistent, round-the-clock medical care.
quick_facts: New financing framework targets 30% of health facilities
Initiative aims to improve patient care nationwide
